blocks.content: Quiz: For a "Read more" section that expands and collapses smoothly, why is it better to toggle a CSS class instead of setting element.style.height directly in JavaScript?
Tap an option below to answer:
Changing styles this way does not affect loading speed. The benefit is structure and maintainability.
Changing styles this way does not affect loading speed. The benefit is structure and maintainability.
So we can use a CSS transition and let the browser handle the animation while keeping styling inside CSS.
JavaScript changes the state by toggling a class. CSS handles how that state looks and animates.
JavaScript changes the state by toggling a class. CSS handles how that state looks and animates.
So screen readers can detect the content.
Accessibility is important, but that is not the main reason for choosing classes here.
Accessibility is important, but that is not the main reason for choosing classes here.
So the button text can change between "Read more" and "Show less."
The button text can change either way. The key advantage is separating behavior from styling.
